extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, chemists, and learned readers interested in the foundations of chemistry/natural philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for judging theories about the elemental/principial constitution of bodies (e.g., Aristotelian four elements, Paracelsian tria prima): what counts as proof, explanatory adequacy, and useful experimental practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical experiments must actually evince the claimed conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The experiments wont to be brought, whether by the common Peripateticks, or by the vulgar Chymists, to demonstrate that all mixt bodies are made up precisely either of the four Elements, or the three Hypostatical Principles, do not evince what they are alledg'd to prove.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept experimental demonstrations that merely appear relevant; require that the experiment directly and competently prove the specific metaphysical/chemical claim. The author criticizes many published experiments as weak, precarious, or inconclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain causes and manners of production, not only where a quality 'resides'
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘What is it to me to know, that such a quality resides in such a Principle, whilst I remain altogether ignorant of the Cause of that quality, and the manner of its production and Operation?’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A satisfactory theory must give the causal mechanism for properties (e.g., why a substance is purgative), not merely assign the property to a named principle (salt, sulfur, mercury). Practical efficacy is insufficient as philosophical explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid false dichotomies; allow many competing hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Many questions, and especially in matters Physiological, may admit of so many Differing Hypotheses, that ’twill be very inconsiderate and fallacious to conclude (except where the Opinions are precisely Contradictory) the Truth of one from the falsity of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat debate as if only two alternatives exist (e.g., Aristotelian vs. Paracelsian). Consider multiple plausible explanations and test between them rather than inferring truth by elimination without precise contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for motion, texture, and arrangement of small parts, not only material ingredients
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest part of the affections of matter, and consequently of the Phænomena of nature, seems to depend upon the motion and the continuance of the small parts of Bodies...the texture of the Body upon which the moving parts strike, that modifies to motion or Impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanations should include structure, figure, and motion of small corpuscles; many phenomena (e.g., colours, electrical attraction) are better explained by texture/arrangement than by mere presence/proportion of material principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities like colour or smell are insufficient as proofs of elemental identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Qualities he Mentions as Colours, Smels, and the like, belong not to the Elements; they therefore must to the Chymical Principles, he takes that for granted, which will not in haste be prov’d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show colours can be produced or removed by heat/texture without adding or subtracting 'principles' (e.g., quicksilver changing colour in flame, steel showing transient colours). Using such qualities alone to identify elemental composition is unreliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and independence of phenomena from added substances
rubrics_metrics.description: I have here a lasting Colour Generated and Destroy’d (as I have seen) at pleasure, without adding or taking away either Mercury, Salt, or Sulphur...the same body...may exhibite successively divers Colours...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust phenomena that occur without addition or subtraction of putative principles count against the claim that such principles are the source of those phenomena. Demonstrations should be reproducible and not contingent on hidden additives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat chymical separations as proof of pure elementary bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when there intervenes a Chymical resolution by the Fire, ’tis seldom in the Saline or Sulphureous principle, as such, that the desir’d Faculty of the Concrete Resides; But, as that Titular Salt or Sulphur is yet a mixt body, though the Saline or Sulphureous Nature be predominant in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious: substances obtained by distillation or fire are often still mixed/composite; assuming they are pure elements is unwarranted. Purification can remove useful 'accidents' and render products less efficacious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method-independence requirement for elemental identification
rubrics_metrics.description: As the distinct substances whereinto the Alkahest divides bodies, are affirm’d to be differing in nature from those whereunto they are wont to be reduc’d by fire...he could totally reduce all sorts of Stones into Salt only, whereas of a coal he had two distinct Liquors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If different techniques of resolution (fire vs. alkahest) yield different sets of 'principles', then the method, not a true underlying elemental nature, may be determining results. A valid account of elements should not depend on the particular chemical procedure used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality/ubiquity requirement for elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there be any one such body to be constantly met with in all, and each, of those that are said to be Elemented bodies, is the thing I now question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To count as an element in the proposed sense, a body should be regularly present across the mixt bodies it is claimed to compose; sporadic or contingent occurrence weakens the claim that it is a primitive element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow that number/composition of components may vary between concretes
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Concretes affordding more of them than others do; Nay and sometimes this or that Body affording a greater number of Differing substances by one way of management, than the same yields by another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume a fixed small number of universal elements (e.g., exactly four or three); empirical evidence suggests variability among substances and dependence on how they are divided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish practical operativity from philosophical explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: It will but appear That it is useful to Apothecaries, rather than to Philosophers, The being able to make things Operative being sufficient to those, whereas the Knowledge of Causes is the Thing looked after by These.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful preparation or extraction of medicinal/operative products is not equivalent to true understanding of causes. The standards for practitioners (utility) differ from those for philosophers (causal explanation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject arguments grounded on unreasonable or precarious suppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Other common arguments, pretended to be drawn from Reason in favour of Aristotelian Hypothesis...are Commonly grounded upon such unreasonable or precarious Suppositions, that ’tis altogether as easie and as just for any man to reject them, as for those that take them for granted to assert them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand that theoretical premises be reasonable and demonstrable; avoid building conclusions on shaky assumptions or rhetorical inferences lacking solid support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity requirement: show that elements are necessary for nature's compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: The one, that it is necessary that Nature make use of Elements to constitute the bodies that are reputed Mixt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond showing decomposition, one should show that elements are necessary components in nature's processes of composition (e.g., that nature cannot produce mixtures without those elements). Observations of growth from water or other examples that suggest Nature composes without pre-existing elements challenge this necessity claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory comprehensiveness: tria prima insufficient for many qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: I am inclin’d upon this ground to Think, That the artificial resolution of compound bodies by Fire does not so much enrich mankind, as it divides them into their supposed Principles...that the Tria Prima...are far from being able to explicate by any of the Tria Prima, those qualities which they pretend to belong primarily unto it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A satisfactory theory must be capable of explicating a wide range of observed qualities (colour, medicinal virtue, electrical attraction, etc.); the tria prima (salt, sulphur, mercury) fail to provide intelligible accounts for many phenomena.
